prize_parts.citation: for showing how firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting shape international trade, aggregate productivity and the gains from openness

statement.case_for: Firm heterogeneity and selection changed the unit of analysis in trade from the industry to the firm. It explains who exports, who invests abroad, and how openness reallocates resources toward more productive firms. The framework is both a conceptual advance and an empirical one: it is the standard foundation for work on firm-level data across many countries and for quantitative evaluation of trade policy. More than two decades of replication and extension support its durability. Melitz (2003) is the core model, and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) extend it to exporting versus foreign direct investment. The case therefore rests on a dated, checkable and cumulative body of evidence. That is the kind of archive-and-data-driven discovery I value, and it is judged here on the common criteria rather than on field preference.
statement.case_against: Credit is not fully clean. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum contributed the empirical firm-level facts and closely related models, and they are not on the ballot entry. Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are substantial but are left out of my two-name proposal. Helpman is also credited in B001, so the Committee must decide which of his bodies of work it is recognising. Some gains-from-trade results depend on parametric assumptions, such as the distribution of firm productivity. Where firm-level data cannot be tested directly, the quantitative welfare claims are less secure than the qualitative mechanism.

responses.point: Ranks B001 first, arguing that the Grossman-Helpman political-economy work on trade protection is a clean, jointly credited pair with decades of confirmation, and that firm heterogeneity is a different strand of Helpman's work.
responses.response: I agree the Grossman-Helpman attribution is cleaner than the B020 attribution, and that maturity is not an issue for either. I still rank B020 higher because of what each contribution changed. Protection-for-sale is an influential theory, but, as you and others note, its empirical support is mixed. Firm heterogeneity changed measurement, data use and quantitative policy evaluation, and it has held up across many data sets. Cleaner credit does not make a contribution larger. The Helpman overlap means B001 is a close alternative for me, and I would not call the choice lopsided.

responses.point: Supports B001 partly because trade has had no prize since 2008, and treats the firm-heterogeneity strand as a separate contribution that is not needed for the Grossman-Helpman case.
responses.response: The point that trade has not been recognised since 2008 is true, but it applies equally to B020, so it does not favour one trade candidate over the other. It is a field-balance argument, not a scientific one, and I do not weigh it as merit. I agree the strands are distinct, which is why I would keep them as separate decisions. Since the Committee can honour Helpman for only one body of work in a single award, the question is which strand contributed more. On the evidence in the openings, I think it is the firm-level framework.

responses.point: Also ranks B020 first, but flags a real attribution gap: the empirical firm-level foundations from Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited, and Redding is later and more derivative.
responses.response: I share this reservation and have made it my main concern about the case. The three-name cap and the ballot's credited list limit what the Committee can do. Within that list, Melitz and Helpman are the most defensible pair, because Melitz (2003) is the model at the centre and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) is the key extension. I would not treat Redding's quantitative work as equally foundational, and I would not read the Bernard-Eaton-Kortum gap as grounds for rejecting the contribution. It is a reason to word the citation around the mechanism, not around priority.

responses.point: Ranks B001 first on the strength of a broad, durable explanatory framework with a clean two-person credit, and notes that Helpman's firm-heterogeneity work on the list adds to that case.
responses.response: I accept that the Helpman overlap makes B001 and B020 closer than the vote counts suggest, and that B001 draws wider support across the Committee. I do not read breadth of support as scientific merit. The same Helpman overlap means I would rather settle the framing now than leave it to be resolved by default. I keep B001 as a named alternative because it is a serious one, though it is not the one I rank first.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum as co-originators and whether a two-name award would be seen as incomplete.
Whether Helpman's credit is better placed with Melitz (B020) or with Grossman (B001), given that the two strands overlap on him.
How far the quantitative gains-from-trade results depend on parametric assumptions about the productivity distribution.
My knowledge of the finer priority claims comes from memory and the openings, and I have not independently verified it.
statement.conflict_note: none apparent from the supplied profile; no credited candidate on B020 is a Lund colleague, co-author or institutional connection of mine, and I note only that Tommy Andersson is a Lund colleague.
